correctness.rationale: Exact rational denominator-clearing for a general simple quadratic conjugates the Jacobi and cyclic updates to monomial maps. Their transformed ratio laws r->r^3 and r->r^4 give exact closed iterates. Inverting the root coordinate proves the two basins and the dimensionless leading logarithmic error coefficient; a unit-modulus ratio cannot approach root values. Explicit primitive-root constructions yield all least periods m>=2 and tangent-return eigenvalues 1 and q^m. The proof handles poles and collisions by its forward-regular hypothesis. The standalone SymPy and exact-Fraction verifier checks both map identities, invariants, matrix spectra and native iterates, but its finite checks are not extrapolated into an infinite proof.

None of the accessible, materially inspected primary statements implies the shared root-ordering criterion across respective forward-regular domains, fourth-power law, rate coefficient and all-prime-period Floquet multipliers. Searches for formulas, aliases and both update schemes identified no covering result. A forthcoming lower-degree treatment and unindexed classical source remain explicit risks, so this is a supported best-knowledge originality judgment, not priority certification.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial simultaneous-root problem admits an exact whole-basin classification for two practically used update modes. It settles natural algorithmic questions—do both variants obey the same generic cross-ratio separator despite different finite-pole exceptions, what is the sharp full-orbit rate under cyclic reuse, and can degree two have attracting nonroot cycles?—rather than choosing a contrived slice or arbitrary numerical parameter. Its exact root-ratio separation and fourth-power convergence coefficient offer a baseline for precision and update-order analysis. It is restricted to two simple roots, not a claim about more general polynomial degree or floating-point solvers.
